content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines introduction to django forms as part of forms and user input. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Purpose of forms; User input and server-side validation; Form classes; Fields and widgets; Binding data to forms. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Purpose of forms
items.text: Purpose of forms shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

items.title: User input and server-side validation
items.text: User input and server-side validation should be planned for the actual hosting topology: configuration, permissions, resource limits, observability, rollback/recovery and a testable operating procedure all matter.

items.title: Form classes
items.text: Form classes shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

items.title: Fields and widgets
items.text: Fields and widgets affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Binding data to forms
items.text: Binding data to forms affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Introduction to Django Forms
content_blocks.code:
from django import forms

class ContactForm(forms.Form):
    name = forms.CharField(max_length=80)
    email = forms.EmailField()
    message = forms.CharField(widget=forms.Textarea)
content_blocks.expected_output: The form defines server-side validation for required name, email syntax, and message input.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: Always validate on the server. Add abuse controls, accessible error rendering, and CSRF protection in a POST view.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
